recipes.name: 1-Dish Taco Bake
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup masa corn flour OR corn meal
0.75 cup very warm milk (120 degrees F to 130 degrees F)

steps.text: Brown ground beef and drain. Add taco seasoning and mix well.
Mix batter ingredients together in a pre-sprayed 9-1/2-inch deep dish pie plate.
Top batter with taco meat filling. Pour salsa evenly over meat; sprinkle with shredded cheese and corn chips.
Bake by placing in a COLD oven; set temperature to 350 degrees F. Bake for 30 minutes or until done.

raw_recipe.headline: 1-Dish Taco Bake
raw_recipe.description: Here's a one-dish family pleaser with all your favorite Mexican ingredients--salsa, cheese, taco seasoning and corn chips.

review.reviewBody: I doubled everything and put it into a 9x13 pan. I also added a can of beans in chili sauce on top of the meat. Increase baking time to allow for extra size. YUM!

My family really liked this. I used the cornbread recipe on the package of Indian Head corn meal, except I used all cornmeal and no flour, baking powder instead of yeast, 2 eggs. The cornbread was moist. I also used an extra 1/2 cup of cheese and skipped the chips. A 10 inch, deep dish pie plate held everything, but I baked it on a cookie sheet just in case. Everyone said this was a keeper!

I wasn't sure if we were supposed to make the ground beef as directed on the taco mix package, but that is what I did. I used a seasoning packet and the 3/4 cup of water it calls for, and let it boil then simmer for 10 minutes as called for. If I had not done this, it would have been WAY too dry. I think the recipe should be a bit more specific regarding this. EDIT: I have made this recipe at least a dozen times since I first came upon it. I double it and bake it in a 13x9" pan, but use 1 1/2lbs of beef. I use either taco-seasoned beef or sloppy joes beef. My family actually prefers this with a sloppy joe beef mixture. I do add extra salsa, and I am very careful not to overcook it. I think these 2 things help keep it moist and prevent it from being dry (as well as being sure to stick it in a cold oven, and making sure the milk is the proper temperature). We LOVE this recipe.

I made this in my cast iron frying pan and the bottom crust was excellant it had a nice crispy crust . I grated monteray jack cheese over the meat and used a cheddar on the top over the chips. My family loved this and I will definately make it again.

I added minced onion and crushed Fritos to the dough and I let it rise and baked the dough for 15 minutes before adding the filling, then finished baking. I also used beans and corn rather than ground beef. Avocado was nice as one of the toppings. Everyone loved it and wanted the recipe.

Made it according to the directions except I left out the cheese and added a can of black beans. I served it with mixture of finely chopped lettuce, tomato, cilantro and avocado mixed together with lime juice. Those that wanted dairy added sour cream. My husband requested this again. I was unsure how much bulk yeast to add (i never buy packets) so I put 2 teaspoons of the rapid rise yeast in the batter and mixed in a bowl. Then spread it in a larger pie plate. It almost over flowed.

This was GREAT! I doubled the recipe and put it in my lasagna pan. I added corn on top of the meat before I put the salsa and cheese on. I didn't put the corn chips on, I put them on the side and just added them when we put the food on our plate because I knew we would have leftovers and I didn't think the corn chips would be very good warmed up and soggy. Will be making this again!!!

I'm giving this five stars because it's everything the recipe says it is. It's a little heavy for me, but that's personal taste. It was very easy to make. I used the Qorn brand soy-based ground beef substitute, that worked great. ALSO I got home and realized I didn't have any quick-rise yeast. I used 1 tsp of baking soda + 1 1/2 tsp baking powder instead, and that worked just fine. The cornbread base rose well and tasted good. I made it in a 9x9 inch square baking pan and had no overflow. Were I to make this again, I'd probably try less cheese and meat (or whatever) and add beans and corn, maybe some cilantro.

I have made this recipe almost ten times now... Love it! Forget the yeast, it's not important. You can make the cornbread as the box indicates, and use that for the crust without the added ngredients, if you wish. I add salsa to the top before baking, so the favors soak in better. DEFINITELY serve with sour cream!

Hooray!! My kids LOVED it, and it was soooo easy. I used leftover veggi taco meat. Instead of the corn bread topping, I used just a regular flour. Also used leftover tortilla chips (which I was happy to have a use for instead of them going stale). Very tasty.
This was very good. I made it as stated in the recipe, except I did use a larger dish. It would have been too much for a pie dish.
Delicious! I topped it with a dollop of sour cream and Amish corn salsa. :0)
My family of 5 love it, especially my picky 5 year old son.
The crust is a great base, but I made it as written and found that the ratio between crust & toppings wasn’t balanced. Next time I will add more toppings, but I will definitely make it again.
This is one of my family's favorites! I could say we were having this every night and they wouldn't complain.
My family and I love this dish!
We made this with ground turkey and that is why it might've been a little dryer so if you use turkey I would recommend to use more salsa and more cheese.
It was "OK".... one of those once-in-a-while type of dishes. Not that great as leftovers (soggy).

I MADE THIS FOR SUPPER LAST NIGHT. WE ALL REALLY LOVED IT. I WAS NOT PLEASED WITH THE DOUGH.I ALSO ADDED A CAN OF BEANS TO STRETCH IT A BIT. COOKING TIME HAD TO BE INCREASED. THINK I WILL USE 1/2 RECIPE FOR CORNBREAD NEXT TIME.
easy and tastes good
